note: Commerce round 3 (part A): introduction to commerce, occupation, production, factors of production, trade, home trade and business documents, foreign trade, retail and wholesale trade, channels of distribution, transportation, communication and warehousing - scenario items with an invoice passage and a balance-of-payments passage.

passages.title: Invoice received by Ada Fashion Stores
passages.text:
Ada Fashion Stores, Enugu, received the
following invoice from Kano Textiles Ltd.

Invoice No. 0417     Date: 3 March 2026
Your order No. 88 of 20 February 2026
Item                Qty   Unit price
Ankara, 6 yards     100     ₦4,000
Lace, 5 yards        40     ₦9,000
Less trade discount          10%
Terms: 5% cash discount if paid
within 7 days; otherwise net 30 days.
Carriage paid.     E. & O.E.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If Ada Fashion Stores pays the invoice on 20 March 2026, the amount payable is
questions.explanation: Trade discount of 10% (₦76,000) is deducted on the invoice: ₦760,000 − ₦76,000 = ₦684,000. Payment on 20 March is after 7 days, so no cash discount applies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If Ada Fashion Stores pays on 8 March 2026, it pays
questions.explanation: Payment within 7 days earns the 5% cash discount on ₦684,000, i.e. ₦34,200; the amount paid is ₦649,800.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: 'Carriage paid' on the invoice means that
questions.A: Ada Fashion Stores must pay the transporter on delivery of the goods
questions.B: Kano Textiles Ltd bears the cost of transporting the goods to Enugu
questions.C: the goods will be collected from the seller's warehouse by the buyer
questions.D: the transport cost has been added to the invoice total to be paid
questions.explanation: Carriage paid means the seller pays the cost of delivery; carriage forward would make the buyer pay.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Five pieces of lace arrived damaged and were returned. Kano Textiles Ltd should send Ada Fashion Stores
questions.A: a credit note for ₦45,000
questions.B: a debit note for ₦45,000
questions.C: a credit note for ₦40,500
questions.D: an invoice for ₦40,500
questions.explanation: Returned goods are credited at the invoiced (net) price: 5 × ₦9,000 = ₦45,000 less 10% trade discount = ₦40,500, shown on a credit note.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The document Ada Fashion Stores sent to Kano Textiles Ltd on 20 February 2026 was
questions.A: an advice note
questions.B: a quotation
questions.C: a statement of account
questions.D: an order
questions.explanation: The invoice quotes 'Your order No. 88 of 20 February 2026'; the buyer places an order and the seller responds with goods and an invoice.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Country Z's balance of trade in 2025 was
questions.A: a surplus of $7 billion
questions.B: a deficit of $7 billion
questions.C: a deficit of $4 billion
questions.D: a surplus of $11 billion
questions.explanation: Balance of trade = visible exports − visible imports = 45 − 52 = −$7 billion, an unfavourable (deficit) balance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The balance of invisible trade of Country Z was
questions.A: a surplus of $4 billion
questions.B: a deficit of $11 billion
questions.C: a surplus of $11 billion
questions.D: a surplus of $21 billion
questions.explanation: Invisible receipts = 12 + 9 = 21; invisible payments = 8 + 2 = 10; invisible balance = +$11 billion.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Country Z's current account balance for 2025 was
questions.A: a surplus of $11 billion
questions.B: a deficit of $4 billion
questions.C: a deficit of $7 billion
questions.D: a surplus of $4 billion
questions.explanation: Current account = balance of trade + invisible balance = −7 + 11 = +$4 billion, a surplus.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Remittances received from citizens working abroad are recorded in the accounts of Country Z as
questions.A: a visible export
questions.B: an invisible export
questions.C: a visible import
questions.D: an invisible import
questions.explanation: Money earned abroad and sent home is a receipt from foreigners without any goods crossing the border, so it is an invisible export.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: If Country Z wished to turn its balance of trade into a surplus, the most appropriate measure would be to
questions.A: buy more shipping and insurance services from companies based abroad
questions.B: increase the remittances paid out to foreign workers living in the country
questions.C: promote exports of goods and restrict non-essential imports through tariffs and quotas
questions.D: reduce the sale of banking and tourism services to foreigners
questions.explanation: The balance of trade concerns visible goods only; raising exports or cutting imports of goods is what improves it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cocoa farmer in Ondo sells his beans to a licensed buying agent, who sells them to an exporter in Lagos. A shipping line carries the beans to Amsterdam and an insurer covers them for the voyage. Of all these activities, the one that is NOT part of commerce is
questions.A: insuring the cargo for the voyage
questions.B: buying by the licensed agent
questions.C: carriage by the shipping line
questions.D: growing the cocoa on the farm
questions.explanation: Growing cocoa is extractive industry (production). Buying, selling, transport and insurance are trade and aids to trade, which make up commerce.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Commerce is best described as the study of
questions.A: the manufacture of finished goods from raw materials in factories and workshops
questions.B: the distribution and exchange of goods and services, together with the activities that assist them
questions.C: the rendering of direct personal services such as teaching, nursing and hairdressing
questions.D: the management of a country's revenue, taxation and public spending by the government
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade (buying and selling) and the aids to trade such as banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication and advertising.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which pair consists only of aids to trade?
questions.A: retailing and wholesaling
questions.B: mining and fishing
questions.C: banking and warehousing
questions.D: farming and manufacturing
questions.explanation: Banking and warehousing assist trade; retailing and wholesaling are trade itself; mining, fishing, farming and manufacturing are industry.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bakery in Aba produces 5,000 loaves a day but can sell only 800 in its own shop. The commercial activity that would most directly solve this problem is
questions.A: changing the recipe so that the bread tastes better
questions.B: buying a bigger oven so as to raise daily output further
questions.C: employing more bakers to work on the night shift
questions.D: distribution through wholesalers and retailers in other towns
questions.explanation: The bakery's problem is distribution, not production; commerce links producers to consumers through the channel of distribution.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Tourism is regarded as an aid to trade mainly because it
questions.A: extracts minerals and timber from the natural environment for export
questions.B: earns foreign exchange and creates demand for transport, hotels and local goods
questions.C: converts raw materials into finished goods for sale in foreign markets
questions.D: provides free entertainment to citizens during the public holidays
questions.explanation: Tourism brings visitors whose spending stimulates trade in transport, hospitality, crafts and other goods and services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader in Onitsha buys textiles from a Lagos importer and sells them in her shop, using a bank loan, a haulage company and an insurance policy along the way. The banking, transport and insurance services she used are collectively called
questions.A: extractive industry
questions.B: home trade
questions.C: aids to trade
questions.D: direct services
questions.explanation: Aids to trade are the services that make buying and selling possible: banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication, advertising and tourism.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main difference between commerce and industry is that
questions.A: industry deals only with services while commerce deals only with goods
questions.B: industry is carried on by the government while commerce is private
questions.C: commerce produces goods while industry deals with their transport
questions.D: industry produces goods while commerce distributes and exchanges them
questions.explanation: Industry (extractive, manufacturing, constructive) creates goods; commerce moves them from producers to consumers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following best explains why commerce expanded after the introduction of money?
questions.A: Money made it possible to grow more food on the same piece of farm land
questions.B: Money removed the need for a double coincidence of wants, making exchange easier
questions.C: Money made transport by rail and road free of charge for every trader
questions.D: Money forced every producer to consume everything that he produced
questions.explanation: Under barter each trader had to find someone who wanted his goods and had what he wanted; money made exchange quick and general.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The functions of commerce include all of the following EXCEPT
questions.A: the provision of a link between producers and consumers
questions.B: the movement of goods from producers to consumers
questions.C: the conversion of raw cotton into cloth in a textile mill
questions.D: the creation of employment in trade and its aids
questions.explanation: Turning cotton into cloth is manufacturing, an industrial activity; the others are functions of commerce.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A country with good roads, reliable electricity, honest courts and a stable currency will attract more commercial activity because these are
questions.A: direct personal services to consumers
questions.B: examples of aids to trade in the strict sense
questions.C: branches of the extractive industry
questions.D: factors that promote the growth of commerce
questions.explanation: Infrastructure, a stable currency, security and the rule of law are conditions that encourage trade, though they are not themselves aids to trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Home trade differs from foreign trade in that home trade
questions.A: requires import licences, customs duties and foreign exchange
questions.B: takes place within the borders of one country and uses one currency
questions.C: is carried out only by the government of the country
questions.D: involves goods only, whereas foreign trade involves services only
questions.explanation: Home (internal or domestic) trade is buying and selling within a country; foreign trade crosses national borders and involves different currencies.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A student says 'commerce is just buying and selling'. The best correction is that commerce
questions.A: includes only foreign trade and not the trade within the country itself
questions.B: is really the same thing as manufacturing goods in factories and workshops
questions.C: also includes the aids to trade such as banking, insurance, transport and advertising
questions.D: refers only to the activities of the stock exchange and the commercial banks
questions.explanation: Trade is the core of commerce, but commerce also embraces the services that assist trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following obstacles to trade is removed by warehousing?
questions.A: the risk of loss of goods by fire, theft or accident
questions.B: the distance between producer and consumer
questions.C: the lack of information about goods available
questions.D: the time gap between production and consumption
questions.explanation: Warehousing stores goods until they are needed, bridging time; transport bridges distance, advertising bridges lack of knowledge and insurance covers risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The obstacle of consumers' lack of knowledge about a new product is chiefly overcome by
questions.A: insurance
questions.B: advertising
questions.C: warehousing
questions.D: banking
questions.explanation: Advertising informs consumers that a product exists, what it does and where to buy it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Insurance is an aid to trade because it
questions.A: carries goods from the place of production to the place of sale
questions.B: provides the buildings in which goods are stored before they are sold
questions.C: removes the fear of loss and so encourages people to take business risks
questions.D: supplies the money that traders need to buy their opening stock
questions.explanation: By compensating for insured losses, insurance gives traders confidence to invest and to move goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A characteristic of commerce that distinguishes it from a direct service is that commerce
questions.A: cannot be carried on without the use of computers and the internet
questions.B: is always provided free of charge to the whole community by the government
questions.C: requires a university degree from every person who takes part in it
questions.D: is concerned with goods and the services that help their exchange, not personal skill
questions.explanation: Direct services (doctors, lawyers, barbers) sell personal skill; commerce deals with the exchange of goods and the aids to that exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Police officers, soldiers and civil servants render services to the community as a whole rather than to identified individuals. Their occupations are classified as
questions.A: direct services
questions.B: indirect services
questions.C: commercial occupations
questions.D: constructive occupations
questions.explanation: Indirect services benefit society generally; direct services such as those of a doctor or lawyer are rendered to particular persons.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a constructive occupation?
questions.A: refining crude oil at Warri
questions.B: mining tin on the Jos Plateau
questions.C: building the Second Niger Bridge
questions.D: selling cement in a shop
questions.explanation: Constructive occupations build roads, bridges, dams and houses; mining is extractive, refining is manufacturing and selling is commercial.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A man quarries granite, another crushes it into chippings at a plant, and a third uses the chippings to build a road. Their occupations are, in order,
questions.A: extractive, commercial and constructive
questions.B: constructive, extractive and manufacturing
questions.C: manufacturing, commercial and extractive
questions.D: extractive, manufacturing and constructive
questions.explanation: Quarrying takes material from nature (extractive), crushing processes it (manufacturing) and road building is constructive.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A market woman who buys tomatoes from farmers in Kano and sells them in Enugu is engaged in a
questions.A: manufacturing occupation
questions.B: commercial occupation
questions.C: direct service
questions.D: extractive occupation
questions.explanation: Buying and selling goods is trade, which is a commercial occupation.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following workers is NOT engaged in an industrial occupation?
questions.A: a rice farmer
questions.B: a welder in a shipyard
questions.C: a bank cashier
questions.D: a bricklayer
questions.explanation: Banking is an aid to trade (commercial occupation); welding, farming and bricklaying are industrial (manufacturing, extractive, constructive).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Occupations are classified into industrial, commercial and service occupations according to
questions.A: the location where the work is done
questions.B: the income earned by the worker
questions.C: the number of hours worked per week
questions.D: the nature of the work done
questions.explanation: The classification depends on what the worker does: produce goods, exchange goods or render services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A soldier paid by the federal government and a lawyer who charges fees to private clients are both engaged in
questions.A: commercial occupations, since both are paid in money
questions.B: service occupations, though one is indirect and the other direct
questions.C: industrial occupations, since both produce a visible result
questions.D: extractive occupations, since both draw on natural talent
questions.explanation: The soldier renders an indirect service to the community; the lawyer renders a direct service to individual clients.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Poultry farming, fishing and lumbering belong to the same group of occupations because they all
questions.A: distribute goods to final consumers
questions.B: change raw materials into finished goods
questions.C: obtain products directly from nature
questions.D: render services directly to individuals
questions.explanation: They are extractive (primary) occupations, which take products from land, water and forests.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A factory that assembles imported parts into television sets is engaged in
questions.A: constructive production
questions.B: extractive (primary) production
questions.C: tertiary production
questions.D: manufacturing (secondary) production
questions.explanation: Assembling components into finished goods is manufacturing, the secondary stage of production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a tertiary occupation?
questions.A: growing rice in Kebbi
questions.B: operating a haulage company
questions.C: weaving cloth in Abeokuta
questions.D: drilling for crude oil in Bayelsa
questions.explanation: Tertiary occupations provide services such as transport, banking and trade; the others are primary or secondary.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A graduate who cannot find paid employment starts making and selling liquid soap at home. In terms of occupation, she has moved from
questions.A: direct services into indirect services
questions.B: commerce into the extractive industry
questions.C: unemployment into manufacturing and commerce
questions.D: industry into the civil service
questions.explanation: Making soap is manufacturing (industry) and selling it is trade (commerce).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Interdependence among occupations means that
questions.A: no occupation can be carried on in a rural area
questions.B: every worker must hold two jobs at the same time
questions.C: the government must own all businesses in the country
questions.D: each occupation depends on the products or services of others
questions.explanation: A farmer needs the blacksmith's hoe and the trader's market; the trader needs the farmer's crops and the transporter's lorry.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A journalist, an accountant and a computer programmer earn their living mainly by
questions.A: extracting raw materials from the earth
questions.B: selling their skills as direct services
questions.C: buying and reselling goods for profit
questions.D: constructing roads, bridges and houses
questions.explanation: These are professional (direct) services rendered to clients or employers for a fee or salary.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Specialisation among occupations is made possible chiefly by
questions.A: the abolition of foreign trade
questions.B: government control of prices
questions.C: the existence of money and exchange
questions.D: the size of a country's army
questions.explanation: A person can concentrate on one occupation only if he can exchange his output or wages for the other things he needs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In commerce, production is regarded as complete only when goods
questions.A: are advertised on television
questions.B: leave the factory gate
questions.C: are stored in a warehouse
questions.D: reach the final consumer
questions.explanation: Production is the creation of utility, and utility is not fully realised until the goods are in the hands of the consumer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A farmer harvests cassava, a processor turns it into garri, a transporter carries it to the city, and a retailer sells it. The transporter and the retailer are
questions.A: not producers because they make nothing
questions.B: engaged in tertiary production
questions.C: engaged in primary production
questions.D: engaged in secondary production
questions.explanation: Tertiary production consists of the services (transport, trade, banking) that bring goods to the consumer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Production creates form, place, time and possession utility. Storing yams from harvest until the lean season creates
questions.A: place utility
questions.B: form utility
questions.C: time utility
questions.D: possession utility
questions.explanation: Making goods available at the time they are wanted creates time utility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A carpenter turning planks into chairs creates
questions.A: possession utility
questions.B: time utility
questions.C: place utility
questions.D: form utility
questions.explanation: Changing the form of a material to make it more useful creates form utility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: When a retailer sells a phone to a customer and hands it over, the utility created is
questions.A: form utility
questions.B: possession utility
questions.C: time utility
questions.D: place utility
questions.explanation: Transferring ownership of goods to the person who wants them creates possession utility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of indirect production?
questions.A: a man building a hut for himself on his farm
questions.B: a woman cooking dinner for her own family
questions.C: a tailor sewing clothes to sell to the public
questions.D: a boy fetching water for his own bath
questions.explanation: Indirect production is production for exchange; direct production is producing for one's own use.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A shoe factory employs one worker to cut leather, another to stitch, another to fix soles and another to polish. This arrangement is
questions.A: diversification
questions.B: vertical integration
questions.C: mass consumption
questions.D: division of labour
questions.explanation: Splitting a job into separate tasks, each done by a different worker, is division of labour.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A disadvantage of division of labour to the worker is that
questions.A: output per worker falls sharply over time
questions.B: repeating one small task all day becomes monotonous
questions.C: the worker must buy all his own tools
questions.D: the worker can never be replaced by another
questions.explanation: Repetitive work causes boredom and loss of pride in the finished product; it also makes workers easy to replace.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Division of labour is limited mainly by
questions.A: the number of banks in the town
questions.B: the height of the factory building
questions.C: the size of the market for the product
questions.D: the age of the factory owner
questions.explanation: Specialisation pays only if enough units can be sold; a small market cannot absorb large specialised output.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Large-scale production usually lowers the cost per unit because
questions.A: workers in large firms are never paid overtime
questions.B: the government pays part of the wages of large firms
questions.C: large firms do not pay for their raw materials
questions.D: fixed costs are spread over a greater number of units
questions.explanation: Spreading rent, machinery and management costs over more units gives economies of scale.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A rancher in Adamawa rears cattle, a factory in Kano cans the beef, a trader sells the tins and a lorry carries them to Lagos. The rancher's activity is
questions.A: secondary production
questions.B: primary production
questions.C: tertiary production
questions.D: indirect production
questions.explanation: Primary (extractive) production obtains raw materials and food directly from nature; canning is secondary, trade and transport tertiary.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The stage of production in which raw materials are transformed into finished or semi-finished goods is
questions.A: tertiary production
questions.B: primary production
questions.C: secondary production
questions.D: direct production
questions.explanation: Manufacturing and construction make up secondary production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company that grows sugar cane on its own plantation, refines the sugar in its own mill and sells it through its own shops is engaged in
questions.A: indirect services at every stage of the process
questions.B: primary production at every stage of the process
questions.C: tertiary production at every stage of the process
questions.D: primary, secondary and tertiary production
questions.explanation: Growing cane is primary, refining is secondary and retailing is tertiary production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mechanisation in production is likely to
questions.A: reduce output while increasing the number of workers needed
questions.B: increase output and reduce the number of unskilled workers needed
questions.C: leave output unchanged but double the cost per unit
questions.D: make division of labour impossible in the factory
questions.explanation: Machines raise output per worker, so fewer hands are needed for the same or greater output.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which factor is most likely to limit large-scale production of yam flour in a small town?
questions.A: the presence of a good road to the town
questions.B: the availability of yams in the area
questions.C: a small market that cannot absorb the output
questions.D: the existence of a bank in the town
questions.explanation: The extent of the market limits the scale of production and of division of labour.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A farmer pays ₦50,000 a year for the use of a plot of land, ₦200,000 in wages to his labourers and ₦30,000 as interest on a bank loan. The three payments are the rewards of
questions.A: entrepreneur, land and capital respectively
questions.B: capital, land and labour respectively
questions.C: labour, capital and land respectively
questions.D: land, labour and capital respectively
questions.explanation: Rent is the reward of land, wages of labour and interest of capital; profit is the reward of the entrepreneur.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is classified as capital in production?
questions.A: a river used for fishing
questions.B: a tractor used on a farm
questions.C: a farmer's own labour
questions.D: the sunshine that ripens crops
questions.explanation: Capital is man-made wealth used in further production; rivers and sunshine are land (gifts of nature).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The factor of production that bears the risk of the business and receives profit is
questions.A: capital
questions.B: labour
questions.C: the entrepreneur
questions.D: land
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur organises the other factors, takes decisions and bears the risk of loss in return for profit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Land as a factor of production includes
questions.A: the money paid to acquire a plot of land
questions.B: only the soil used for growing crops
questions.C: the buildings erected on a plot by the owner
questions.D: all natural resources such as forests, rivers and minerals
questions.explanation: In economics and commerce 'land' means all free gifts of nature, not just the soil.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mrs Okafor combined ₦2 million of her savings, a rented shop and two employees to start a bakery, taking the risk that it might fail. Mrs Okafor is functioning as
questions.A: labour
questions.B: an entrepreneur
questions.C: capital
questions.D: land
questions.explanation: Combining the factors of production and bearing the risk is the role of the entrepreneur.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A university lecturer's monthly salary is the reward for the factor of production called
questions.A: land
questions.B: capital
questions.C: labour
questions.D: enterprise
questions.explanation: Wages and salaries are the reward for labour, whether physical or mental.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which feature distinguishes land from the other factors of production?
questions.A: it receives profit as its reward
questions.B: it can be increased by saving and investment
questions.C: it is mobile and can be moved from place to place
questions.D: its total supply is fixed and it is a gift of nature
questions.explanation: Land is geographically immobile, fixed in supply and not man-made; capital is man-made and can be increased.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Capital differs from land in that capital
questions.A: is a free gift of nature to every producer
questions.B: is man-made and can be increased by saving
questions.C: is fixed in total supply for all time
questions.D: receives rent as its reward for production
questions.explanation: Capital (machines, buildings, tools) is produced by man and grows when people save and invest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bus conductor in Ibadan trains as an electrician and takes a job with a construction firm in the same city. He has shown
questions.A: the immobility of labour
questions.B: geographical mobility of labour
questions.C: occupational mobility of labour
questions.D: the mobility of capital
questions.explanation: Occupational mobility is a change of job or trade; geographical mobility is a change of place.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A skilled machine operator in Kano refuses to accept a better-paid job in Lagos because of family ties. This illustrates a barrier to
questions.A: the division of labour
questions.B: occupational mobility of labour
questions.C: the mobility of capital
questions.D: geographical mobility of labour
questions.explanation: Family ties, housing and language are obstacles to the geographical mobility of labour.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The efficiency of labour can be raised by all of the following EXCEPT
questions.A: training and education of workers
questions.B: reducing the wages paid to workers
questions.C: good working conditions and welfare
questions.D: the use of better tools and machines
questions.explanation: Lower wages reduce motivation; training, good conditions and better equipment raise efficiency.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Working capital, as distinct from fixed capital, consists of
questions.A: land and permanent structures
questions.B: buildings, machinery and vehicles
questions.C: cash, stock and debtors used in day-to-day trading
questions.D: the entrepreneur's skill and experience
questions.explanation: Working (circulating) capital is used up or changes form in the course of trading; fixed capital is used repeatedly.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following would be regarded as a factor of production rather than a product of production?
questions.A: a bottle of soft drink
questions.B: bread sold in a shop
questions.C: a shirt bought by a consumer
questions.D: a lorry used by a distributor
questions.explanation: A lorry used in business is capital, a factor of production; the other items are consumer goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Trade is best defined as
questions.A: the production of goods in factories
questions.B: the buying and selling of goods and services
questions.C: the storage of goods in warehouses
questions.D: the transport of goods by road and rail
questions.explanation: Trade is exchange; production, storage and transport are industry or aids to trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Kano trader sells leather bags to a shop in Abuja; another sells the same bags to a shop in Accra, Ghana. The two transactions are, respectively,
questions.A: retail trade and wholesale trade
questions.B: foreign trade and home trade
questions.C: home trade and foreign trade
questions.D: entrepot trade and home trade
questions.explanation: Trade within Nigeria is home trade; a sale to a buyer in Ghana is foreign (export) trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The two main divisions of home trade are
questions.A: barter trade and credit trade
questions.B: import trade and export trade
questions.C: entrepot trade and bilateral trade
questions.D: wholesale trade and retail trade
questions.explanation: Home trade is divided into wholesale (selling in bulk to traders) and retail (selling in small units to consumers).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Import trade, export trade and entrepot trade are the three divisions of
questions.A: home trade
questions.B: foreign trade
questions.C: retail trade
questions.D: wholesale trade
questions.explanation: Foreign trade consists of import, export and entrepot (re-export) trade; home trade is divided into wholesale and retail.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Bilateral trade is trade
questions.A: within one country
questions.B: among many countries at once
questions.C: between two countries only
questions.D: between a wholesaler and a retailer
questions.explanation: Bilateral means two-sided; multilateral trade involves many countries.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Under barter, a yam farmer who wants a goat must find a goat owner who wants yams. This difficulty is called
questions.A: absence of deferred payment
questions.B: indivisibility of goods
questions.C: lack of a store of value
questions.D: double coincidence of wants
questions.explanation: Each party must want exactly what the other offers; money removes this difficulty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Trade makes it possible for a country to
questions.A: produce everything its people need
questions.B: consume goods it cannot produce itself
questions.C: avoid the use of money completely
questions.D: keep all its goods within its borders
questions.explanation: Through trade, countries exchange their surpluses for goods they cannot produce or produce only at high cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a reason why countries trade with one another?
questions.A: differences in skills and technology
questions.B: differences in climate and natural resources
questions.C: every country can produce all goods at the same cost
questions.D: the desire to sell surplus output abroad
questions.explanation: Trade arises precisely because countries differ in resources, skills and costs of production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Multilateral trade exists when
questions.A: goods are exchanged without the use of money
questions.B: a country trades with one partner only
questions.C: trade takes place only within a region of a country
questions.D: many countries trade with one another
questions.explanation: Multilateral trade involves several countries buying from and selling to one another.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Counter-trade, in which a country exchanges crude oil directly for machinery from another country, is a modern form of
questions.A: hire purchase
questions.B: barter
questions.C: entrepot trade
questions.D: retail trade
questions.explanation: Exchanging goods directly for goods without money changing hands is barter, even between governments.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer wants to know the prices and terms at which a wholesaler will supply goods before placing an order. He should send
questions.A: a credit note
questions.B: an invoice
questions.C: a letter of enquiry
questions.D: a receipt
questions.explanation: The enquiry asks for information; the seller replies with a quotation, catalogue or price list.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: In reply to an enquiry, a supplier sends a document stating prices, discounts and delivery terms. This document is
questions.A: a delivery note
questions.B: a debit note
questions.C: a statement of account
questions.D: a quotation
questions.explanation: A quotation states the terms on which the seller is willing to supply the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A buyer who is satisfied with a quotation then sends the seller
questions.A: an invoice
questions.B: an order
questions.C: a receipt
questions.D: a credit note
questions.explanation: The order instructs the seller to supply the goods described at the quoted terms.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler under-charged a retailer by ₦5,000 on an invoice. To correct the error he sends
questions.A: a receipt for ₦5,000
questions.B: a credit note for ₦5,000
questions.C: a debit note for ₦5,000
questions.D: a fresh quotation
questions.explanation: A debit note increases the amount the buyer owes; a credit note reduces it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A document that accompanies goods and is signed by the buyer as proof that the goods were received is
questions.A: an order form
questions.B: an advice note
questions.C: a consignment note
questions.D: a delivery note
questions.explanation: The delivery note lists the goods delivered; the buyer signs a copy which the seller keeps as evidence of delivery.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A supplier sends a note to a customer informing him that goods have been dispatched and should arrive soon. This document is
questions.A: a delivery note
questions.B: an advice note
questions.C: a credit note
questions.D: an invoice
questions.explanation: The advice note is sent ahead of the goods so that the buyer can prepare to receive them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An invoice bears the letters 'E. & O.E.' This means the seller
questions.A: has already received payment in full
questions.B: will not accept the return of the goods
questions.C: may correct any errors or omissions found later
questions.D: will pay the cost of carriage
questions.explanation: 'Errors and omissions excepted' reserves the seller's right to correct mistakes on the invoice.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer in Jos receives goods from a Lagos supplier marked 'carriage forward'. When the transporter arrives, the retailer must
questions.A: pay the supplier an extra 10% on the invoice
questions.B: refuse the goods until the supplier pays the transporter
questions.C: return the goods to the supplier at his own expense
questions.D: pay the transporter the cost of carrying the goods
questions.explanation: Carriage forward: the buyer pays the transporter on arrival; carriage paid: the seller has already paid.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A price list marked 'ex-warehouse' means the price
questions.A: includes delivery to the buyer's own premises
questions.B: excludes the cost of moving the goods from the seller's warehouse
questions.C: includes insurance and freight to the buyer's town
questions.D: is only valid if the buyer pays cash on delivery
questions.explanation: Ex-warehouse (or ex-works) prices cover the goods only; the buyer arranges and pays for carriage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader who receives a cash discount of 2½% on an invoice of ₦400,000 pays
questions.explanation: 2½% of ₦400,000 is ₦10,000, so the trader pays ₦390,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: 'C.O.D.' on a contract of sale means
questions.A: the goods are sent free of charge
questions.B: the buyer pays before the goods are sent
questions.C: the seller allows three months' credit
questions.D: the buyer pays when the goods are delivered
questions.explanation: Cash on delivery: the carrier collects payment when handing over the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: 'C.W.O.' (cash with order) protects the seller because
questions.A: he can charge interest on the unpaid balance
questions.B: he receives payment before releasing the goods
questions.C: the buyer must collect the goods himself
questions.D: the goods remain his property after delivery
questions.explanation: Cash with order means the buyer pays when ordering, so the seller bears no credit risk.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The purpose of a trade discount is to
questions.A: compensate the buyer for goods that arrived damaged
questions.B: reward the buyer for paying his account promptly
questions.C: enable the retailer to sell at the list price and still make a profit
questions.D: cover the cost of transporting the goods to the buyer
questions.explanation: Trade discount is given by a manufacturer or wholesaler to a trader off the list price; the trader's margin lies in that discount.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Unlike a trade discount, a cash discount
questions.A: increases with the quantity of goods bought
questions.B: is deducted on the invoice before the total is calculated
questions.C: is given to all buyers regardless of when they pay
questions.D: is given only when payment is made within a stated period
questions.explanation: Cash discount rewards prompt payment and is deducted at the time of payment, not on the invoice.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A quantity discount is given to a customer who
questions.A: pays for goods in cash
questions.B: buys goods in large quantities
questions.C: collects goods from the seller's warehouse
questions.D: returns damaged goods
questions.explanation: Quantity (bulk) discount encourages large orders, which cut the seller's costs per unit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A receipt is a document which
questions.A: corrects an overcharge on an invoice
questions.B: requests payment for goods supplied
questions.C: acknowledges that payment has been received
questions.D: lists goods available for sale
questions.explanation: The receipt is the buyer's evidence of payment; the invoice requests payment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler sends his customers a document at the end of every month showing the goods supplied, payments received and the balance owing. A retailer who finds the closing balance too high should check it against
questions.A: the order forms he sent at the start of the month
questions.B: the supplier's catalogue and current price list
questions.C: the delivery notes signed by the supplier's driver
questions.D: the invoices and credit notes received during the month
questions.explanation: The statement of account summarises invoices, credit notes and payments; comparing it with those documents reveals any error.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A pharmacy buys drugs with a list price of ₦250,000. The wholesaler allows 20% trade discount and 5% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If the pharmacy pays on the tenth day, the amount paid is

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following documents is NOT used in home trade?
questions.A: credit note
questions.B: invoice
questions.C: bill of lading
questions.D: delivery note
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is a shipping document used in foreign trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A catalogue differs from a price list in that a catalogue
questions.A: shows the balance owed by each customer at the end of the month
questions.B: is sent only to foreign buyers, while a price list is for home buyers
questions.C: is a binding legal contract, while a price list is not
questions.D: describes and often illustrates the goods, while a price list shows only prices
questions.explanation: A catalogue gives descriptions and pictures of goods; a price list simply states current prices.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A buyer received goods worth ₦60,000 that he had not ordered and returned them. The seller should issue
questions.A: a debit note for ₦60,000
questions.B: a credit note for ₦60,000
questions.C: an invoice for ₦60,000
questions.D: a receipt for ₦60,000
questions.explanation: Returns reduce the amount owed by the buyer, and the seller records the reduction on a credit note.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Terms of payment on an invoice read 'Net 30 days'. This means
questions.A: payment must be made in 30 monthly instalments
questions.B: a 30% discount is allowed for prompt payment
questions.C: the full amount is due within 30 days with no discount
questions.D: the goods must be returned within 30 days
questions.explanation: 'Net' means no further discount; the invoice total must be paid within 30 days.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An invoice serves the buyer chiefly as
questions.A: an offer that he is free to reject
questions.B: proof that the goods have been paid for
questions.C: a title document that can be sold to a bank
questions.D: a record of the goods bought and the amount owed
questions.explanation: The invoice shows quantities, prices, discounts and the total due; the receipt is the proof of payment.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Nigerian importer of machinery from Germany must usually obtain, before shipment, a document that authorises the importation. This document is
questions.A: a bill of lading
questions.B: an import licence
questions.C: a certificate of origin
questions.D: a consular invoice
questions.explanation: An import licence (or import permit) is the government's authority to bring specified goods into the country.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A document certifying the country in which goods were produced, often needed to claim preferential customs duty within ECOWAS, is
questions.A: an indent
questions.B: a bill of lading
questions.C: a certificate of origin
questions.D: a charter party
questions.explanation: The certificate of origin shows where goods were made, which determines the rate of duty under trade agreements.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An importer in Lagos orders goods through an agent abroad by sending a document that specifies the goods, quantity and price. This document is
questions.A: a freight note
questions.B: a bill of sight
questions.C: a dock warrant
questions.D: an indent
questions.explanation: An indent is an order sent to an agent abroad; it may be open (agent chooses supplier) or closed (supplier named).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bill of lading is important to an importer because it
questions.A: shows the exchange rate at which the goods were bought
questions.B: serves as a document of title enabling him to claim the goods from the ship
questions.C: guarantees that the goods are of merchantable quality
questions.D: exempts the goods from customs duty on arrival
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is a receipt, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title to the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods sent by air are covered by
questions.A: a charter party
questions.B: a bill of lading
questions.C: an airway bill
questions.D: a mate's receipt
questions.explanation: The airway bill is the air-transport equivalent of the bill of lading, though it is not a document of title.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A contract by which an exporter hires a whole ship to carry his cargo is
questions.A: a letter of hypothecation
questions.B: a bill of lading
questions.C: a consular invoice
questions.D: a charter party
questions.explanation: A charter party hires a ship for a voyage or a period of time.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods quoted 'F.O.B. Apapa' means the price includes
questions.A: freight and insurance to the buyer's port of destination
questions.B: all costs up to loading the goods on board the ship at Apapa
questions.C: customs duty payable at the port of destination
questions.D: delivery to the buyer's own warehouse
questions.explanation: Free on board: the seller's responsibility ends once the goods are on the ship; the buyer pays freight and insurance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An importer who has not received full documents and cannot describe the goods exactly may enter them at customs on
questions.A: a bill of exchange
questions.B: a bill of entry
questions.C: a bill of sight
questions.D: a bill of lading
questions.explanation: A bill of sight allows the goods to be examined so that a full entry can be made later.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A ship's manifest is
questions.A: a licence to import restricted goods
questions.B: a receipt for goods placed in a bonded warehouse
questions.C: an order to pay the exporter a stated sum
questions.D: a list of all the cargo carried by a ship
questions.explanation: The manifest lists every consignment on board and is presented to customs at the port.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A quota, as an instrument of trade policy, is
questions.A: a tax on goods brought into the country
questions.B: a limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported
questions.C: a total ban on the import of a good
questions.D: a subsidy paid to exporters
questions.explanation: A quota restricts quantity; a tariff is a tax; an embargo is a ban.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following would improve Nigeria's balance of trade?
questions.A: an increase in Nigerians' holidays abroad
questions.B: an increase in imports of cars
questions.C: an increase in exports of cocoa and sesame
questions.D: a fall in the price of crude oil exports
questions.explanation: The balance of trade improves when visible exports rise relative to visible imports.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A country's balance of payments records
questions.A: the amount of foreign currency held by the central bank
questions.B: only the value of its visible exports and imports
questions.C: the total revenue collected by the customs service
questions.D: all its receipts from and payments to other countries in a year
questions.explanation: The balance of payments covers visible and invisible trade and capital movements; the balance of trade covers goods only.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Payments for shipping, insurance, tourism and banking services between countries are recorded as
questions.A: visible trade
questions.B: invisible trade
questions.C: entrepot trade
questions.D: bilateral trade
questions.explanation: Services do not pass through customs as goods do, so they are 'invisible' items.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Nigerian importer agrees to pay a Chinese exporter 90 days after the goods are shipped. The exporter draws a document ordering the importer to pay the sum on that date. This document is
questions.A: a letter of credit
questions.B: a promissory note
questions.C: a bill of exchange
questions.D: a bank draft
questions.explanation: A bill of exchange is an unconditional written order by the creditor requiring the debtor to pay a stated sum at a fixed date.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Dumping occurs when
questions.A: a country bans the export of raw materials
questions.B: imported goods are destroyed by customs officers
questions.C: goods are stored in a bonded warehouse without paying duty
questions.D: goods are sold abroad at a price lower than in the home market
questions.explanation: Dumping is selling exports below the home price or below cost, which can harm producers in the importing country.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Excise duty differs from customs duty in that excise duty is levied on
questions.A: goods imported into the country
questions.B: goods produced within the country
questions.C: goods exported from the country
questions.D: goods passing through the country in transit
questions.explanation: Excise duty is charged on home-produced goods such as beer and cigarettes; customs duty on imports and exports.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main function of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) is to
questions.A: fix the exchange rate of the naira
questions.B: collect customs duties on imports at the ports
questions.C: encourage and assist the export of non-oil products
questions.D: grant import licences to manufacturers
questions.explanation: NEPC promotes and develops non-oil exports through incentives, information and training.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A consular invoice is
questions.A: a bill drawn by the exporter on the importer's bank for the price
questions.B: a receipt issued by the port authority when goods are landed from a ship
questions.C: a document showing that freight has been paid in full to the carrier
questions.D: an invoice certified by the importing country's consul, stating the true value of the goods
questions.explanation: The consul's certification helps the importing country's customs to assess duty correctly and prevent dumping.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an invisible export of Nigeria?
questions.A: cocoa beans sold by Nigerian farmers to the Netherlands
questions.B: fees earned by Nigerian banks from foreign customers
questions.C: crude oil sold by Nigeria to refineries in India
questions.D: second-hand cars imported into Nigeria from Japan
questions.explanation: Services sold to foreigners earn foreign exchange without goods leaving the country; they are invisible exports.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) promotes trade among members mainly by
questions.A: banning trade between members and countries outside the region
questions.B: fixing a single price for all goods sold in West Africa
questions.C: removing tariffs and other barriers on goods produced within the region
questions.D: printing a common currency that is already used in every member state
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme allows qualifying goods to move among member states free of duty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An 'ex-ship' price quoted to an importer covers
questions.A: the customs duty payable at the destination port only
questions.B: only the cost of the goods at the exporter's own factory gate
questions.C: the cost of transporting the goods from the port to the buyer's premises
questions.D: all costs until the goods are available on board at the port of destination
questions.explanation: Ex-ship: the seller bears all costs and risks until the ship reaches the destination port; unloading and duty are for the buyer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods imported into Nigeria and kept in a bonded warehouse may be re-exported
questions.A: only after import duty has been paid
questions.B: without payment of import duty
questions.C: only after being processed
questions.D: only if they are perishable
questions.explanation: Duty is paid only when goods are withdrawn for home use; goods re-exported from bond attract no duty.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Terms of trade refer to
questions.A: the discount allowed on a foreign invoice
questions.B: the conditions attached to a letter of credit
questions.C: the ratio of a country's export prices to its import prices
questions.D: the period of credit allowed to an importer
questions.explanation: Terms of trade improve when export prices rise relative to import prices.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Nigerian trader who wants to buy goods from a supplier in Brazil finds that the supplier speaks Portuguese, quotes in dollars and follows different commercial laws. These difficulties illustrate
questions.A: divisions of international trade
questions.B: advantages of international trade
questions.C: aids to international trade
questions.D: barriers to international trade
questions.explanation: Different currencies, languages, laws and tariffs make foreign trade more difficult than home trade.
