questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer who moves from street to street selling bread from a tray on his head is
questions.A: a mail-order retailer
questions.B: a stall holder
questions.C: a hawker
questions.D: a departmental store owner
questions.explanation: Hawkers and pedlars are itinerant small-scale retailers with no fixed premises.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the retailer to the consumer?
questions.A: storing goods for the wholesaler at the retailer's own expense
questions.B: manufacturing goods according to the consumer's own specification
questions.C: providing finance to the manufacturer for large-scale production
questions.D: breaking bulk and selling in small quantities convenient to the consumer
questions.explanation: The retailer buys in bulk from the wholesaler and sells in units the consumer can afford and use.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A small shop owner buys goods on credit from a wholesaler and gives credit to trusted customers in her neighbourhood. This shows that the small-scale retailer
questions.A: always sells at lower prices than large stores
questions.B: gives personal service and credit that large stores rarely give
questions.C: buys directly from foreign manufacturers
questions.D: does not need any capital to start business
questions.explanation: Personal attention, credit and nearness to customers are the main strengths of the small retailer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Small-scale retailers survive in Nigeria despite competition from supermarkets mainly because they
questions.A: advertise heavily on radio and television
questions.B: buy directly from foreign manufacturers at lower prices
questions.C: sell in very small units, give credit and are located close to customers
questions.D: are exempted by law from paying any taxes
questions.explanation: Selling a single cube of seasoning or a sachet of milk near the customer's home meets needs supermarkets do not serve.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retail outlet that sells a wide range of food and household goods on a self-service basis with customers paying at check-out counters is
questions.A: a specialty shop
questions.B: a mail-order house
questions.C: a mobile shop
questions.D: a supermarket
questions.explanation: Supermarkets are large self-service stores selling mainly food and household items.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer who sells goods through a catalogue and delivers them by post or courier operates
questions.A: a chain store
questions.B: a mail-order business
questions.C: a department store
questions.D: a market stall
questions.explanation: Mail-order retailers have no shop; customers order from catalogues or online and goods are delivered.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A 'multiple shop' (chain store) is characterised by
questions.A: the sale of goods by post from a catalogue
questions.B: a single very large building divided into departments
questions.C: many branches selling similar goods under centralised buying and control
questions.D: a van that carries goods to villages on market days
questions.explanation: Multiple shops have several branches with the same name, layout and goods, controlled from a head office.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Under a deferred payment (credit sale) arrangement, unlike hire purchase, the buyer
questions.A: can return the goods at any time and stop paying the remaining instalments
questions.B: never becomes the owner of the goods at any stage of the payment period
questions.C: must pay the whole price in cash before he is allowed to take the goods
questions.D: becomes the owner of the goods immediately, even though he pays by instalments
questions.explanation: In a credit sale ownership passes at once; under hire purchase it passes only when the last instalment is paid.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A furniture shop sells a set costing ₦300,000 cash on hire purchase for a deposit of ₦60,000 and 12 monthly instalments of ₦25,000. The hire-purchase charge is

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer's mark-up is 25% on cost. Her margin on selling price is
questions.explanation: If cost is 100, selling price is 125 and gross profit 25; margin = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Automatic vending machines are most suitable for selling
questions.A: goods that require demonstration
questions.B: expensive goods such as cars
questions.C: perishable goods such as fresh fish
questions.D: small standardised goods such as drinks and snacks
questions.explanation: Vending machines sell low-priced, uniform, pre-packed items without a sales assistant.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A department store differs from a supermarket in that a department store
questions.A: sells goods only by self-service with no attendants at all
questions.B: sells a wide variety of goods in separate departments, often with personal service
questions.C: sells only foodstuffs and household consumables
questions.D: operates from a vehicle that moves from place to place
questions.explanation: Department stores are 'many shops under one roof' with sales assistants; supermarkets are self-service and food-based.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: One advantage of large-scale retailing is that
questions.A: very little capital is needed to start and run the business
questions.B: the owner knows every customer personally and gives them credit
questions.C: bulk buying earns large trade discounts, allowing lower prices
questions.D: there is no need for any advertising or window display at all
questions.explanation: Large retailers buy directly from manufacturers in bulk and pass some of the savings to customers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A disadvantage of a department store is that
questions.A: customers are not allowed to see the goods before buying
questions.B: it cannot offer more than one type of goods
questions.C: it is always situated in a village
questions.D: it needs large capital and high running costs, so prices may be high
questions.explanation: Prime city sites, large staff and elaborate buildings make department stores costly to run.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The practice of selling a few well-known items at a loss to attract customers who then buy other goods is called
questions.A: price skimming
questions.B: loss-leader pricing
questions.C: dumping
questions.D: resale price maintenance
questions.explanation: The loss leader draws customers into the shop, where profits are made on other purchases.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Branding and pre-packaging by manufacturers have reduced the importance of the retailer's function of
questions.A: locating the shop close to where the customers live
questions.B: giving credit to regular customers who are known to him
questions.C: weighing, measuring and packing goods for customers
questions.D: offering after-sales service on the goods he sells
questions.explanation: Pre-packed branded goods arrive ready for sale, so the retailer no longer weighs and wraps them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A supermarket turns over its stock 10 times a year and its average stock at cost is ₦150,000. Its cost of goods sold for the year is
questions.explanation: Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold ÷ average stock, so cost of goods sold = 10 × ₦150,000 = ₦1,500,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A discount store is a retail outlet that
questions.A: discounts bills of exchange for traders who need cash before maturity
questions.B: sells branded goods below the usual retail price by keeping its costs low
questions.C: gives loans to small retailers at rates of interest below the bank rate
questions.D: sells goods only to registered members who pay a yearly subscription
questions.explanation: Discount stores offer few services and simple premises so that they can undercut other retailers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Franchising, as used by fast-food chains, allows the franchisee to
questions.A: sell any goods he likes under his own name
questions.B: own shares in the franchisor's company automatically
questions.C: use the franchisor's name, products and methods in return for a fee
questions.D: obtain goods free of charge from the franchisor
questions.explanation: The franchisee runs his own outlet under the franchisor's brand and system, paying an initial fee and royalties.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a common reason for the failure of small retail shops?
questions.A: locating the shop close to the customers in a residential area
questions.B: too much capital and too many trained staff for the size of the shop
questions.C: buying goods at very large trade discounts from the wholesalers
questions.D: poor record-keeping and mixing business money with personal money
questions.explanation: Many small traders fail because they draw business cash for private use and keep no proper records.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Consumer cooperative shops differ from other retail outlets in that
questions.A: they are owned by the government and sell at controlled prices
questions.B: they are owned by their customers, who share the surplus according to their purchases
questions.C: they sell only to wholesalers and never to consumers
questions.D: they are owned by manufacturers who sell only their own brands
questions.explanation: Members own the shop, each has one vote and the surplus is returned as a patronage dividend.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer displays goods attractively in the shop window and arranges them neatly on shelves. The purpose is to
questions.A: satisfy the requirements of the tax authority
questions.B: reduce the shop's electricity bill
questions.C: attract customers and increase sales
questions.D: comply with the Sale of Goods Act
questions.explanation: Display is a form of sales promotion at the point of sale.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer's selling price for a bag of rice is ₦90,000 and his mark-up is 20% on cost. The cost price is
questions.explanation: Selling price = cost × 1.2, so cost = ₦90,000 ÷ 1.2 = ₦75,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler helps the retailer chiefly by
questions.A: manufacturing goods to the retailer's specification
questions.B: breaking bulk and supplying small quantities near the retailer's shop
questions.C: advertising the retailer's shop on television
questions.D: selling directly to the retailer's customers
questions.explanation: The wholesaler buys in bulk from many producers and sells smaller lots to retailers, often on credit.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler's function of holding stock helps to
questions.A: reduce the variety of goods available to consumers
questions.B: increase the price of goods to consumers
questions.C: stabilise prices by releasing goods gradually to the market
questions.D: eliminate the need for retailers
questions.explanation: By storing goods when supply is high and releasing them when it is low, wholesalers even out prices.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A manufacturer of sugar can plan production evenly through the year although demand is seasonal because
questions.A: the government fixes the price of sugar
questions.B: consumers buy sugar only in December
questions.C: retailers pay in advance for a year's supply
questions.D: wholesalers buy and store the sugar until it is needed
questions.explanation: Wholesalers relieve the manufacturer of storage and allow continuous production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Cash-and-carry wholesalers differ from traditional wholesalers in that they
questions.A: give long credit and free delivery to retailers
questions.B: sell only for cash and do not deliver goods to retailers
questions.C: sell directly to final consumers only
questions.D: operate only in foreign trade
questions.explanation: Retailers pay cash and carry the goods away themselves, so prices are lower.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler who takes possession of goods and sells them on behalf of a manufacturer for a commission, without owning them, is
questions.A: a rack jobber
questions.B: a merchant wholesaler
questions.C: a factor
questions.D: a retailer
questions.explanation: A factor is an agent who holds the goods and may sell in his own name; a merchant wholesaler buys and owns the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A rack jobber is a wholesaler who
questions.A: buys goods at public auction for resale to retailers in other countries
questions.B: sells goods to farmers only in rural markets on the days the markets are held
questions.C: exports goods on behalf of the government and is paid a fixed commission
questions.D: stocks and services display racks in supermarkets and is paid for goods actually sold
questions.explanation: Rack jobbers stock and maintain racks of specialised goods in retail stores, which pay only for what is sold.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The wholesaler passes information about consumer preferences from retailers to
questions.A: customs officers
questions.B: manufacturers
questions.C: bankers
questions.D: insurers
questions.explanation: As the link between retailers and producers, the wholesaler tells manufacturers what consumers want.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following situations makes the elimination of the wholesaler possible?
questions.A: goods being bought by thousands of small scattered retailers
questions.B: a manufacturer producing very small quantities of many different goods
questions.C: a manufacturer producing goods to the order of a few large retailers
questions.D: goods that need to be stored for a long time before sale
questions.explanation: Large retailers buying directly in bulk can perform the wholesaler's functions themselves.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler who imports goods and sells them to retailers in the home country is
questions.A: a broker
questions.B: an export merchant
questions.C: a retailer
questions.D: an import merchant
questions.explanation: Import merchants buy goods abroad in their own name and distribute them to home retailers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: When a manufacturer sells directly to consumers through his own retail shops, the wholesaler is
questions.A: given more work
questions.B: eliminated
questions.C: paid a higher commission
questions.D: converted into a retailer
questions.explanation: Direct selling by the producer cuts out both the independent wholesaler and the independent retailer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler buys 500 cartons of milk at a list price of ₦8,000 per carton with a trade discount of 15% and sells them at ₦9,000 per carton. His gross profit is

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the wholesaler to the manufacturer?
questions.A: the wholesaler prevents retailers from selling the goods
questions.B: the wholesaler sells the goods at a loss so as to increase demand for them
questions.C: the wholesaler makes the goods on behalf of the manufacturer
questions.D: the wholesaler finances the manufacturer by paying promptly for goods bought in bulk
questions.explanation: Prompt payment for large quantities gives the manufacturer working capital to continue production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler who specialises in one line of goods, such as pharmaceuticals, is called
questions.A: a general wholesaler
questions.B: a specialist wholesaler
questions.C: a retailer
questions.D: a broker
questions.explanation: General wholesalers handle many lines; specialist wholesalers concentrate on one class of goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the wholesaler?
questions.A: grading and packaging goods
questions.B: warehousing goods
questions.C: manufacturing goods for retailers
questions.D: giving credit to retailers
questions.explanation: Wholesalers distribute goods; they do not manufacture them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler prepares, grades and packs kolanuts into standard sizes before selling them to retailers. This function is
questions.A: financing the producer
questions.B: breaking bulk
questions.C: risk bearing
questions.D: preparing goods for sale
questions.explanation: Grading, blending, packing and branding make goods ready for retail sale.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler bears risk on behalf of the manufacturer when
questions.A: the manufacturer raises the price of goods after delivery
questions.B: goods he has bought fall in price or go out of fashion before he sells them
questions.C: the retailer buys directly from the manufacturer
questions.D: the government reduces import duty on the goods
questions.explanation: Having bought and paid for the goods, the wholesaler bears the risk of price falls, deterioration and changes in fashion.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The most common channel for the distribution of consumer goods such as detergent is
questions.A: manufacturer to retailer to wholesaler to consumer
questions.B: manufacturer directly to consumer
questions.C: manufacturer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
questions.D: wholesaler to manufacturer to retailer to consumer
questions.explanation: Mass-produced consumer goods normally pass through both a wholesaler and a retailer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cement company appoints Mr Dike to sell its cement in Anambra; he never buys the cement himself but receives 2% of every sale he arranges. Mr Dike is
questions.A: a consumer
questions.B: a merchant wholesaler
questions.C: a retailer
questions.D: an agent
questions.explanation: Agents sell on behalf of a principal for commission without taking ownership; merchant wholesalers buy and own what they sell.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A middleman in the channel of distribution is
questions.A: a worker in the middle of an assembly line
questions.B: any person or firm between the producer and the final consumer
questions.C: a manager who supervises junior staff
questions.D: the customer who buys goods for his own use
questions.explanation: Wholesalers, retailers, agents and brokers are middlemen.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A manufacturer of industrial machinery is most likely to sell
questions.A: through supermarkets
questions.B: through hawkers
questions.C: directly to the industrial users
questions.D: through mail order to households
questions.explanation: Expensive technical goods bought by few customers are sold directly, often with installation and service.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following goods would most likely be distributed through the longest channel?
questions.A: fresh vegetables sold at the farm gate
questions.B: aircraft sold to airlines
questions.C: custom-made furniture
questions.D: matches sold in every village in the country
questions.explanation: Cheap, standardised goods bought by millions of scattered consumers pass through several middlemen.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A factor influencing the choice of a channel of distribution is
questions.A: the colour of the manufacturer's factory building
questions.B: the nature of the product, such as whether it is perishable or bulky
questions.C: the number of banks in the country
questions.D: the age of the managing director
questions.explanation: Perishability, value, bulk, the size of the market and the resources of the producer determine the channel.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Elimination of middlemen may NOT reduce the price to the consumer because
questions.A: the functions of the middlemen still have to be performed by someone at a cost
questions.B: consumers generally prefer to pay higher prices for goods that pass through middlemen
questions.C: the government fixes the prices of all goods whether or not middlemen are used
questions.D: middlemen do not charge anything for the services they render to producers
questions.explanation: Storage, bulk breaking, transport and credit remain necessary; whoever performs them incurs the cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Farmers who sell their tomatoes to consumers at a roadside stall are using
questions.A: a direct (zero-level) channel
questions.B: a two-level channel
questions.C: a three-level channel
questions.D: an agent channel
questions.explanation: No middleman stands between producer and consumer, so the channel is direct.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A broker in the channel of distribution
questions.A: brings buyer and seller together for a commission without handling the goods
questions.B: buys goods in bulk and stores them in his warehouse
questions.C: manufactures goods for sale to wholesalers
questions.D: transports goods from the factory to the retailer
questions.explanation: Unlike a factor, a broker does not take possession of the goods; he negotiates the deal.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advantage of selling through wholesalers rather than directly to retailers is that the manufacturer
questions.A: deals with fewer customers and so reduces selling and distribution costs
questions.B: receives a higher price per unit from wholesalers
questions.C: no longer needs to advertise the product
questions.D: can stop producing goods for stock
questions.explanation: A few large orders from wholesalers are cheaper to handle than thousands of small retail orders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company sells its products through its website and delivers by courier to customers' homes. The channel used is
questions.A: direct selling through e-commerce
questions.B: a channel through wholesalers
questions.C: a channel through agents and brokers
questions.D: an entrepot channel
questions.explanation: Online sales from producer to consumer bypass all middlemen.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A del credere agent is one who
questions.A: guarantees payment for goods sold on credit in return for extra commission
questions.B: sells goods by public auction to the highest bidder
questions.C: clears imported goods through customs for a fee
questions.D: insures goods against loss while in transit
questions.explanation: The del credere agent bears the risk of the buyer's default and earns a higher commission for it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Multi-level (network) marketing distributes products through
questions.A: independent distributors who recruit other distributors and earn commissions
questions.B: government-owned shops in every state, which sell only at controlled prices
questions.C: wholesalers who sell only to supermarkets and never to small retailers
questions.D: auctions held in the manufacturer's factory at the end of every month
questions.explanation: Each distributor sells directly and earns commission on sales made by those he recruits.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A brewery appoints key distributors in each state who buy from it in bulk and supply bars and shops. In the channel of distribution the key distributors act as
questions.A: wholesalers
questions.B: retailers
questions.C: consumers
questions.D: manufacturers
questions.explanation: They buy in bulk from the producer and sell to retailers, which is the wholesaler's role.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A pharmaceutical company must deliver vaccines that need to be kept cold to clinics scattered across a state within a day. The most suitable means is
questions.A: refrigerated road vans
questions.B: rail wagons
questions.C: inland waterways
questions.D: pipeline
questions.explanation: Road transport reaches scattered destinations door to door, and refrigerated vans keep the cold chain.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of road transport over rail transport?
questions.A: it provides door-to-door delivery
questions.B: it carries bulky goods more cheaply over long distances
questions.C: it is less affected by weather and traffic
questions.D: it causes fewer accidents
questions.explanation: Lorries can collect and deliver anywhere there is a road; trains are confined to the track.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Sea transport is most suitable for
questions.A: bulky, heavy goods that are not urgently needed
questions.B: perishable goods needed within hours
questions.C: urgent business documents
questions.D: passengers travelling within a city
questions.explanation: Ships carry huge loads cheaply but slowly.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A tramp ship differs from a liner in that a tramp
questions.A: has no fixed route or timetable and goes wherever cargo is available
questions.B: sails on a fixed route according to a published timetable
questions.C: carries only passengers and mail
questions.D: operates only on inland rivers
questions.explanation: Tramps are chartered as cargo is offered; liners run scheduled services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The document issued by a road haulage firm acknowledging receipt of goods for carriage is
questions.A: a consignment note
questions.B: a bill of lading
questions.C: a charter party
questions.D: an airway bill
questions.explanation: The consignment note is the road (or rail) carrier's receipt and contract of carriage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Containerisation has benefited international trade mainly by
questions.A: reducing handling time, pilferage and damage to goods
questions.B: increasing the number of dock workers needed
questions.C: making it impossible to carry small consignments
questions.D: eliminating the need for ships
questions.explanation: Sealed standard containers move from lorry to ship to train without the goods being handled.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The main disadvantage of air transport is that
questions.A: it is expensive and unsuitable for bulky, low-value goods
questions.B: it is the slowest means of transport for goods and passengers
questions.C: it cannot cross national borders without a customs escort
questions.D: it cannot carry perishable goods such as flowers and fish
questions.explanation: High freight rates and limited capacity confine air freight to light, valuable or urgent goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advantage of pipelines over road tankers for moving petroleum products is that pipelines
questions.A: operate continuously at low running cost once built
questions.B: can carry any type of goods including solids
questions.C: need no capital to construct
questions.D: can be moved easily to a new route
questions.explanation: Pipelines cost much to build but move liquids and gas cheaply, safely and continuously.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following factors is LEAST important in choosing a means of transport?
questions.A: the colour of the goods
questions.B: the cost of carriage
questions.C: the urgency of delivery
questions.D: the nature of the goods
questions.explanation: Cost, speed, safety, nature of goods and distance matter; colour does not.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Inland waterways such as the River Niger are useful for transporting
questions.A: bulky goods cheaply between riverside towns
questions.B: urgent medical supplies
questions.C: passengers in a hurry
questions.D: goods to towns far from any river
questions.explanation: River transport is slow and limited to navigable rivers but very cheap for heavy loads.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Transport creates
questions.A: place utility by moving goods to where they are wanted
questions.B: form utility by changing the shape of goods
questions.C: time utility by storing goods
questions.D: possession utility by advertising goods
questions.explanation: Moving goods from where they are produced to where they are demanded adds place utility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A haulage company charges by weight and distance. Which of the following is a fixed cost to the company?
questions.A: the annual insurance premium on its lorries
questions.B: fuel used on each trip
questions.C: drivers' allowances per trip
questions.D: toll fees paid on each journey
questions.explanation: Insurance, licences and depreciation are paid whether or not the lorries move; fuel and tolls vary with trips.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The transport of goods by rail in Nigeria is limited mainly by
questions.A: the limited network and poor condition of many tracks
questions.B: the high speed of trains
questions.C: the low carrying capacity of wagons
questions.D: the door-to-door service rail provides
questions.explanation: Few lines, old tracks and irregular services restrict rail freight.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of rail transport?
questions.A: it carries heavy and bulky goods over long distances at relatively low cost
questions.B: it provides door-to-door service to every village and hamlet in the country
questions.C: it is the fastest means of transport available for urgent consignments
questions.D: it can change its route at any time to avoid traffic jams and bad roads
questions.explanation: Trains carry large tonnages of cement, grain and containers cheaply over long distances.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A freight forwarder assists an exporter by
questions.A: arranging transport, documentation and customs clearance of goods
questions.B: manufacturing the goods for export
questions.C: buying the goods and reselling them abroad
questions.D: insuring the exporter's factory against fire
questions.explanation: Forwarding agents specialise in moving goods through ports and borders on behalf of shippers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) is responsible for
questions.A: managing seaports and providing port facilities
questions.B: operating all the airlines in Nigeria
questions.C: constructing federal highways
questions.D: issuing driving licences
questions.explanation: NPA manages the ports, quays and harbours through which sea-borne trade passes.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Roll-on roll-off (Ro-Ro) vessels are designed to carry
questions.A: vehicles that are driven on and off the ship
questions.B: crude oil pumped in and out of the ship
questions.C: passengers who board by ladder from boats
questions.D: liquefied gas kept under great pressure
questions.explanation: Ro-Ro ships have ramps so that cars and lorries can be driven aboard.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: For a trader whose goods have a high value in relation to their weight, such as jewellery, the most suitable means of transport is
questions.A: air transport
questions.B: sea transport
questions.C: rail transport
questions.D: pipeline
questions.explanation: Air freight is costly per kilogram, but fast and secure, so it suits light, valuable goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of sea transport?
questions.A: it is slow and unsuitable for highly perishable goods
questions.B: it cannot carry bulky goods
questions.C: it is the most expensive means of transport
questions.D: it cannot be used for international trade
questions.explanation: Voyages take weeks, so fresh goods must go by air or in refrigerated ships.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Transport helps to widen the market for goods because it
questions.A: enables goods to be sold far from where they are produced
questions.B: reduces the quantity of goods produced
questions.C: prevents goods from leaving the factory
questions.D: raises the price of goods in the local market
questions.explanation: Cheap, reliable transport lets producers reach distant customers and so expands the market.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) contributes to transport in Nigeria by
questions.A: enforcing road traffic rules and reducing accidents
questions.B: building railway lines
questions.C: operating the airports
questions.D: collecting customs duty at the ports
questions.explanation: FRSC regulates road use, issues driver's licences and promotes road safety.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company needs to inform 5,000 customers across the country of a change in prices at low cost within a day. The most suitable means is
questions.A: bulk SMS or e-mail
questions.B: registered post
questions.C: personal visits by sales staff
questions.D: telegram
questions.explanation: Electronic messages reach thousands of people instantly at very low cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a means of oral communication?
questions.A: telephone
questions.B: e-mail
questions.C: letter
questions.D: fax
questions.explanation: The telephone carries the spoken word; the others are written communication.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A courier service differs from the ordinary postal service in that a courier
questions.A: collects and delivers door-to-door, usually faster but at a higher charge
questions.B: delivers items only within a single city and never between states
questions.C: is always owned and operated by the federal government
questions.D: carries letters only and does not accept parcels of any size
questions.explanation: Couriers offer speed, tracking and door-to-door service for a premium price.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Video conferencing enables a firm to
questions.A: hold meetings with people in different places without travelling
questions.B: send goods to customers in other towns without using a transporter
questions.C: store goods in distant warehouses without paying any rent
questions.D: print documents in colour in any office it chooses
questions.explanation: Participants see and hear one another over the internet, saving travel time and cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The internet has helped commerce mainly by
questions.A: making it possible to advertise, order and pay for goods online
questions.B: removing the need for transport of goods from producer to consumer
questions.C: abolishing customs duties on all goods imported into the country
questions.D: eliminating all the risks that traders face in doing business
questions.explanation: E-commerce, online advertising and electronic payments all depend on the internet.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is a mass communication medium?
questions.A: television
questions.B: telephone
questions.C: letter
questions.D: memo
questions.explanation: Mass media such as television, radio and newspapers reach large audiences at once.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A memorandum (memo) is used for
questions.A: written communication within an organisation
questions.B: communication with foreign suppliers only
questions.C: advertising to the general public
questions.D: paying for goods bought online
questions.explanation: Memos pass information between departments or staff inside a firm.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) is responsible for
questions.A: regulating telecommunications services in Nigeria
questions.B: delivering letters and parcels throughout Nigeria
questions.C: printing and distributing newspapers in Nigeria
questions.D: operating the federal radio stations in Nigeria
questions.explanation: NCC licenses and regulates telephone and internet service providers.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A business sends an important legal document by registered post rather than ordinary post because
questions.A: registered post provides proof of posting and compensation if the item is lost
questions.B: registered post costs less than ordinary post for every item sent
questions.C: ordinary post is not permitted to carry legal documents of any kind
questions.D: registered post is always delivered by air within the same day
questions.explanation: Registration records the item at every stage and the sender obtains a receipt.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Communication in business is important because it
questions.A: enables buyers and sellers to exchange information about goods, prices and orders
questions.B: removes the need for money in the exchange of goods between buyers and sellers
questions.C: converts raw materials into finished goods that can be sold to the consumers
questions.D: guarantees a profit to every trader who takes part in buying and selling
questions.explanation: Enquiries, quotations, orders and complaints all depend on effective communication.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of visual communication?
questions.A: a chart or poster
questions.B: a telephone call
questions.C: a radio jingle
questions.D: a voice note
questions.explanation: Charts, posters, signs and pictures communicate through sight.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A telephone call to a supplier has an advantage over a letter in that it
questions.A: gets an immediate response
questions.B: provides a permanent written record
questions.C: is always cheaper
questions.D: cannot be misunderstood
questions.explanation: Speech allows instant two-way discussion; a letter provides the record.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Barriers to effective communication in business include
questions.A: the use of technical jargon and poor listening
questions.B: clear language and prompt feedback
questions.C: short messages and good timing
questions.D: the use of the receiver's own language
questions.explanation: Jargon, noise, poor listening and wrong choice of medium prevent messages from being understood.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: NIPOST is the government agency responsible for
questions.A: postal services in Nigeria
questions.B: telecommunications regulation
questions.C: television broadcasting
questions.D: internet banking
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Postal Service handles mail, postal orders and related services.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An e-mail differs from a letter sent by post in that an e-mail
questions.A: is delivered electronically within seconds to any part of the world
questions.B: always requires a postage stamp before it can be sent to the receiver
questions.C: cannot carry attachments such as documents, pictures or videos
questions.D: must be handwritten and signed by the sender before it is sent
questions.explanation: E-mail travels over the internet almost instantly and can carry documents and pictures.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A warehouse owned by a manufacturer and used to store his own goods is
questions.A: a private warehouse
questions.B: a public warehouse
questions.C: a bonded warehouse
questions.D: a state warehouse
questions.explanation: Private warehouses belong to the firm whose goods they hold.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader who does not own a warehouse but rents space to store goods for a fee uses
questions.A: a public warehouse
questions.B: a private warehouse
questions.C: a factory warehouse
questions.D: a retail shop
questions.explanation: Public warehouses let space to any trader who pays the charges.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An importer cannot pay duty on a large consignment at once. To avoid the goods being seized he should
questions.A: keep the goods in a bonded warehouse and pay duty as he withdraws them
questions.B: sell the goods immediately at the port to any buyer who offers cash
questions.C: return the goods to the exporter and ask for his money to be refunded
questions.D: keep the goods in his own private warehouse until he can pay the duty
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses hold dutiable goods under customs control until duty is paid on the portion withdrawn.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods in a bonded warehouse may be
questions.A: re-packed, blended or labelled under customs supervision
questions.B: sold to consumers without paying duty
questions.C: removed at any time without customs permission
questions.D: stored free of charge by the government
questions.explanation: Owners may prepare goods for sale in bond, but nothing leaves for home use until duty is paid.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Warehousing helps to stabilise prices because
questions.A: goods stored can be released gradually to match demand
questions.B: goods in a warehouse cannot be sold
questions.C: warehouses increase the cost of production
questions.D: warehouses reduce the quantity of goods available
questions.explanation: Storage prevents gluts at harvest and shortages later, keeping prices steadier.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following goods most requires a cold-storage warehouse?
questions.A: frozen fish
questions.B: cement
questions.C: textiles
questions.D: iron rods
questions.explanation: Perishable foods must be kept at low temperature to prevent spoilage.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A warehouse keeper issues a document to the owner of goods deposited, which can be transferred to a buyer as evidence of ownership. This document is
questions.A: a warehouse warrant
questions.B: a bill of lading
questions.C: a credit note
questions.D: an invoice
questions.explanation: A warehouse (or dock) warrant is a document of title to goods in store.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Warehousing enables producers of seasonal goods such as rice to
questions.A: make the goods available to consumers throughout the year
questions.B: sell all the rice on the day of harvest
questions.C: avoid the use of transport
questions.D: sell only to the government
questions.explanation: Storage bridges the gap between the harvest season and year-round consumption.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a warehouse?
questions.A: manufacturing goods for sale
questions.B: protecting goods from theft and weather
questions.C: enabling bulk breaking
questions.D: storing goods until they are needed
questions.explanation: Warehouses store, protect and prepare goods; they do not produce them.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler's warehouse close to a city helps retailers because
questions.A: they can replenish their stock quickly in small quantities
questions.B: they no longer need to keep any stock
questions.C: they can buy directly from foreign suppliers
questions.D: they are exempted from paying for the goods
questions.explanation: Nearby stocks let retailers buy little and often, reducing their own storage needs.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: State (government) warehouses are usually located
questions.A: at ports and airports for goods awaiting customs clearance
questions.B: in every village market for goods awaiting sale
questions.C: inside supermarkets for goods awaiting display
questions.D: in private homes for goods awaiting delivery
questions.explanation: Government warehouses at ports hold imported goods until they are cleared.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A firm that keeps large stocks in its warehouse incurs
questions.A: storage costs and the risk of goods deteriorating or going out of fashion
questions.B: no costs at all until the goods are sold
questions.C: lower insurance premiums than firms with no stock
questions.D: customs duty on locally produced goods
questions.explanation: Stock ties up capital and attracts rent, insurance and the risk of loss in value.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Modern warehouses use computers and barcodes mainly to
questions.A: keep accurate records of stock received and issued
questions.B: produce the goods that are stored in the warehouse
questions.C: advertise the stored goods to consumers on television
questions.D: collect taxes from traders on behalf of the government
questions.explanation: Computerised stock control shows what is in store, where it is and when to reorder.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Warehousing and transport are complementary because
questions.A: goods must be stored while awaiting transport and after arrival before sale
questions.B: goods can only be transported by the warehouse owner
questions.C: transport is never needed once goods are stored
questions.D: warehouses replace the need for transport
questions.explanation: Transport moves goods between points; warehouses hold them at those points until they are needed.
